text:
tia-customer: Hey team — our on-prem gateway (customer-managed) suddenly started returning lots of 429s after a traffic spike this morning. We use a k8s NGINX ingress + a sidecar rate-limiter. 429s appear even though upstream pods seem healthy. Any pointers?

jordan-support: Thanks for the report. Quick Qs: is the rate limiter implemented as a leaky-bucket in the sidecar, or are you using an external rate-limit service (Envoy/Redis)? Also which tokens are being exhausted (gateway-level vs per-client)? :eyes:

tia-customer: It's a leaky-bucket in the sidecar (golang lib), plus an Envoy local rate-limit for short windows. We throttle globally at gateway and also per-api-key. Spikes were ~8x normal. 429s logged for a small set of API keys mostly.

ryan-eng-sre: Two quick things to check: 1) kube-proxy/ingress burst window and 2) token refill rate on the leaky bucket. If the refill is tied to a single thread or timer it can lag under CPU pressure. Can you paste the sidecar config?

tia-customer: Pasting the rate limiter YAML snippet: ```yaml
rate_limiter:
  mode: leaky_bucket
  capacity: 1000
  refill_per_sec: 20
  per_key_limit: 200
  global_limit: 5000
  idle_timeout: 30s
```

sophie-eng-platform: That refill_per_sec looks low for an 8x spike. Also how are you calculating bursts from the ingress? NGINX ingress has `limit_req_zone` with a burst param — if that's set small, it will reject before your sidecar ever sees it. Can you show your ingress annotation?

tia-customer: Ingress annotation: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "1000"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "50"` (legacy helm chart).

jordan-support: Ah — that `limit-rps: 50` is per-second and has a very small burst allowance by default. Combined with sidecar refill_per_sec=20 you can easily get 429s during a short surge. Two mitigation paths: raise ingress burst window and increase sidecar refill, or put a short-term buffer in front (small queueing service) so that the leaky-bucket drains smoothly. :+1:

ryan-eng-sre: For quick repro/validation you can simulate a spike with `wrk` or `hey` from inside cluster: `wrk -t2 -c200 -d30s http://<gateway>/predict` to confirm ingress throttling. Also check metrics: ingress `limit_req` counters and sidecar `drop_count`.

tia-customer: Running the replay now — seeing drop_count spike on sidecar, and NGINX `limited` metric increases too. What safe values would you recommend for burst? We don't want to open unlimited bursts and starve downstream.

sophie-eng-platform: Rule of thumb: set ingress burst to 2-3x expected short spike, then tune sidecar refill to match your downstream capacity. Example: if average rps is 200 and worst short spike 1200, set `limit-rps` ~400 with `burst` 800 in ingress, and sidecar `refill_per_sec` ~400-600 with `capacity` sized to hold the burst (e.g., capacity = burst + margin). Also add quick health-check backpressure: if queue > X then start shedding lower-priority keys.

jordan-support: If you use Envoy rate-limiter, you can use local token-bucket with `unit` milliseconds to allow fine-grained refill. For NGINX ingress (nginx-controller) annotations look like: ```yaml
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "400"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "800"
```

ryan-eng-sre: Another operational safeguard: add a short-lived cache of per-key token credits in Redis (atomically increment/expire) so that sudden bursts from a single API key are smoothed across replicas. But beware of extra latency and Redis capacity.

tia-customer: Helpful. One more weirdness — billing shows a drop in token usage corresponding to 429 window (expected) but also a few big spikes after the 429s stop where downstream CPUs max out and requests queue. Is that a backpressure feedback loop?

sophie-eng-platform: Yes — classic backpressure amplification. Gateway returns 429, clients retry aggressively, gateway window reopens, a flood goes through and saturates downstream causing higher latencies and potentially more retries. Mitigate with: 1) exponential backoff on client, 2) jitter, 3) server-side retry quotas per-key with cooldown. Also consider short lived 503 with Retry-After for full-system throttles so clients back off.

jordan-support: For your on-prem context, we recommend these immediate steps: 1) raise ingress `limit-rps` to 3x baseline, set `limit-burst` to expected spike - baseline; 2) increase sidecar `refill_per_sec` accordingly and bump capacity; 3) enable request queuing with small timeout (so you don't queue forever); 4) add a rate-limit telemetry dashboard (ingress + sidecar) and an alert for sustained `limited` > 1% p99 for 5m.

tia-customer: We'll try the config changes. Any quick commands to dump the ingress limiter counters?

ryan-eng-sre: For nginx-ingress-controller you can `kubectl exec` into the controller pod and `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18080/nginx_status` or check prometheus metrics: `nginx_ingress_controller_responses{code="429"}`. For Envoy use admin API: `GET /stats | grep limit` on admin port.

ratebot: alert: gateway-429-spike detected for cluster prod-eu at 2026-03-16T09:12:01Z — 4300 429s in 2m — impacted keys: k-42,k-99

jordan-support: Thanks @ratebot — tia, ping us when you've toggled the limits and run a replay. We'll watch metrics and help dial further. If you want, we can also provision a temporary dedicated capacity on Redwood Dedicated to absorb the spike while you tune on-prem limits.

tia-customer: Will do, thanks all. I'll post results in this thread when done. :bow:
